title: Cooling the City
label: 問6
passageHtml:
Cooling the City

Cities are often warmer than nearby rural areas because roads and buildings absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night. This is called the urban heat island effect.

One response is to plant street trees. Their leaves provide shade, while water released from leaves cools the surrounding air. Yet trees need soil, water, and years to grow. Another option is a “cool roof,” made with a light-coloured surface that reflects more sunlight. Cool roofs can be installed quickly, but they mainly improve the building beneath them and offer little shade at street level.

Some cities also use small “pocket parks” on unused land. These combine plants, seating, and sometimes water features. Their cooling effect may cover only a limited area, but they can also provide places for rest and social contact.
